questions.question: When you are in a travel lane on the road:

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong entrance ramp of the freeway.
Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Continue to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and drive through the intersection.
Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
Drive into the intersection and force the other vehicle to stop.
Honk your horn and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Let that vehicle pass through safely before you proceed.

questions.question: The posted speed limit shows:

options.text: The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed when road and weather conditions are good.
The maximum safe speed under all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed when road and weather conditions are good.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed for that stretch of road. You may need to drive slower than the posted limit. In poor road or weather conditions, slow down.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. What should you do to merge safely into traffic?

options.text: Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before merging to make sure you have a safe space to enter.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When you enter traffic from a driveway or private road, yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when you have a clear space to do so.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, you should:

options.text: Try to get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as he or she passes you.
Speed up as he or she is passing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If you encounter an aggressive driver, move out of their way. Avoid eye contact with a hostile driver. Speeding up may make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Two solid white lines painted across a traffic lane show the boundaries of a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know that:

options.text: Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians are responsible to stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to safely cross. Always stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
Traffic in the lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
Lanes are reserved for buses and vehicles with a driver and one or more passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: How should you change lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one else is moving into the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: What helps ensure safe driving after drinking alcohol socially?

options.text: Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid driving after drinking is to arrange a ride with a sober friend. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your blood. Your body needs about one hour to eliminate one drink of alcohol.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills, curves, or at intersections. Do not pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a road with a median.

questions.question: Where is passing prohibited?
questions.explanation: It is illegal and unsafe to pass on hills, curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.

questions.question: What should you do when it starts to sleet or snow?

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Leave more distance between your vehicle and the car ahead.

questions.explanation: In snow and sleet, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Leave extra distance between your vehicle and others because slippery roads increase your stopping distance.

questions.question: When is it important to slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, near pedestrians or hazards, and on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: What does alcohol cause?
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: What color curb indicates a fire zone with no parking allowed?
questions.explanation: A red curb means no parking in a fire zone.

questions.question: What should you do when a school bus has its stop arm extended?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn and pass on the left.
Continue driving after most children have exited.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has its stop arm extended. Do not move until the stop arm is withdrawn.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger directs you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When red flashing signals and gates are operating.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, when there is a stop sign, or when red flashing signals and gates are operating.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: The highest or lowest speed allowed by law
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed allowed by law
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest safe speed allowed on a road. The top speeds are for perfect conditions. You must slow down when conditions are worse.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: A road joins from the right
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead will turn sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: The best thing you can do to prevent injury or death in a crash is to:

options.text: Stay in the right lane on highways with multiple lanes
Drive only between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single best way to reduce your chance of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol
questions.explanation: Only time will lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not reduce BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they cannot change your BAC.

questions.question: Which describes a defensive driver?
questions.explanation: Defensive drivers have the skills to drive safely through traffic without endangering others. They know the blind spots of other vehicles. A good defensive driver watches the road ahead, avoids distractions, and follows traffic rules.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear before moving

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or leaving a freeway. Before moving right or left, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot is clear.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming
Keep driving since you have the right of way
Stop only if a police officer is nearby
Treat it like a stop sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights warn of dangerous intersections. Treat them like stop signs.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at an intersection with a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Watch what other cars are doing

questions.explanation: Traffic signals keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers must obey these signals. The only exception is when a police officer is directing traffic.

questions.question: Which substances can impair your driving and may lead to a driving under the influence (DUII) arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medicines (both prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread
Inflate your tires to the right pressure
Slow down when driving in rain

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires with good tread and properly inflated. Slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds.

questions.question: What should you do when you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make gestures to show your disapproval.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between your vehicle and theirs. Slow down and let them pass. Do not look at them or make hand gestures.

questions.question: How can you help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
questions.explanation: Road rage is becoming more common as more drivers use the roads. To prevent it, use turn signals properly, obey speed limits, and plan for extra travel time.

questions.question: What should you do if you are in an accident?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people, but help stop severe bleeding by applying pressure. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: What is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can harm an infant or small child, even in a minor crash.
Make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.

questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chance of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under should sit properly restrained in the back seat. Never place a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat if the vehicle has a front airbag.

questions.question: What problems can worn or bald tires cause?
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder. Tires with poor tread also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What is hardest to see at night?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than road signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: What can happen when alcohol is mixed with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both may become stronger.
The effects of both may become weaker.
Only the alcohol effects may become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Alcohol combined with another drug can make the effects of both stronger. For example, one drink plus a cold medicine can affect you like several drinks would.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back.
Continue driving and use the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a last-minute turn at your exit. If you miss it, go to the next exit.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is correct?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous AND speeding can cause death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous AND speeding can cause death.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, the chance of death increases. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, you have almost no chance of surviving a crash. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may take unsafe risks to pass you.

questions.question: How can you avoid a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Avoid driving beside them and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside them and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and back. Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate.
